name: German
review: built 2026-11-12 by Claude Fable 5.2 from the questionnaire answers, lexicon and visible paradigms, after two schedule reads and three blind fluency reads of the rows; 153 of 153 held-out rows pass on the first judged run (tooling/experiments/renderer-process/de-acceptance.md); audited 2026-11-13 by Claude Fable 5.2 against independently computed fire times (about 4,100 patterns), which found wrong schedules the rows had not caught (a run of years said as two years, a nearest-weekday date in months that lack it, an exception beside weekdays) and unholdable lists of years and seconds; the rule book, 46 new hard-case rows and the renderer were amended, and none of the new forms has had a blind fluency read; revised a second time 2026-11-13 by Claude Fable 5.2 with the core's calendar facts (dates no month has, leap years, open year runs, runs and cadences together), a trap list from eight languages, and the German usage notes (usage.md): «Werktag» replaced, «jährlich» before a date fused with its month, a schedule that never runs said as «nie», exceptions kept from covering both sides of a date and a weekday; none of these forms has had a blind fluency read either; 2026-11-13: says when both day fields must match (a day field written from a star beside a restricted one, as in Vixie cron), in rows, rule and renderer written by Claude Sonnet 5.5 from this rule book's seed and reviewed by Claude Fable 5.2; a blind Sonnet reader told these sentences from the union's 16 times of 16, and none has had a blind fluency read; 2026-11-14: a minute of the hour is said by its number as timetables say it («zur Minute 30», «zu den Minuten 5, 20 und 45», «in den Minuten 0 bis 29») and separate hours with listed minutes as hours («um 9, 13 und 17 Uhr, jeweils zu den Minuten 5, 20 und 45»), on the maintainer's decision after blind readers rejected «um :05» and read windows round listed minutes as continuous; rows, rule and renderer by Claude Opus 5.5; three isolated Opus readers checked the new forms, and the second readings they found (a cadence of hours ending «bis 20 Uhr», «sowie» after «jeweils», «außer von 13:05 bis 13:45 Uhr») were removed; the final forms have had no blind fluency read; amended again 2026-11-14 by Claude Opus 5.5 on the maintainer's rulings, on top of the revision for places in the hour: a cadence of hours that comes round the day is said bare («alle 2 Stunden», «alle 3 Stunden zu den Minuten 5, 20 und 45») or with its start only («ab 1:00 Uhr alle 2 Stunden»), with no «täglich», window or series, hours taken out following as an exception; a cadence that does not come round keeps both ends; hours held through each hour are «in den geraden Stunden» or «alle 6 Stunden eine Stunde lang»; the number glosses after odd and even days and hours are gone; seconds beside minute 0 are counted from the full hour; the rule book and the affected rows were rewritten by hand before the renderer changed, and nothing was blind-read; 2026-11-14, released stable on the full reading check: all 706 rows read by three Sonnet 5.5 readers briefed only in the language (5113 questions about moments, scored against an answer key that shares no code with the library), and each of the 4 questions most readers got wrong asked again alone of three Sonnet 5.5 and three Opus 5.5 readers: none was still misread by most readers of both (tooling/scripts/reading/recheck.mjs); 2026-11-19, by Claude Opus 5.5: a step of days that reaches every odd or even day the named months have is said by its word however far the field runs («an den ungeraden Tagen im Juni» for `1-29/2` as for `*/2`), from the core's days reached, so that one schedule is no longer said two ways; the same day, by Claude Opus 5.5: no series is left for the reader to continue (every «…» is gone): a cadence of dates, hours or seconds says its step in words with the ends it has, hours under a finer rhythm as one window and the step a cadence round the day takes, rows rewritten by hand before the renderer; read in full after both changes (739 rows, 5329 questions, three Sonnet 5.5 readers each), none of the 3 questions most readers got wrong was in a changed sentence, and none was still misread alone by most readers of either model (recheck.mjs); the same day: years in step are «in jedem vierten Jahr ab 2028» (no «usw.» series), and no day a firing month lacks is named (a run or step to the longest month's end ends «bis zum Monatsende», listed days only some months have are said with them, a run past February's end carries «(im Februar bis zum Monatsende)»), rows by hand first
